data.body: S1 T3 patterned-fossillike-betafish (0eb8): review-plan PASS signed 0 blocking (2 advisories, P6 prio 0.40 and G6 prio 0.298, both far below their block lines - accepted, recorded for the residual sweep). CLAIMED, implemented, PUSHED as Gerrit 1887. Rebased onto origin/main first, which now carries T2 (binding_store.py 710 LOC) and also 9f7407bb3d 'Isolate nested pytest basetemps' - the landed fix for the macOS flake I recheck'd around, confirming that diagnosis. WORK: (1) Added TWO genuinely-uncovered publication-boundary tests to state/test_binding_retired_commit.py. Existing coverage already had unchanged-pass-no-commit (AC2) and per-file idempotency, and the rotation floors (AC3) are already proven post-delegation because the existing test_get_rotation_heldout.py suite runs THROUGH the now-delegating facade and passed in T2 - so per test-design section 1 I did not duplicate them. The real gaps were AC1's EXCLUSIVITY (nothing asserted the allowlist rejects a non-allowlisted file) and AC4 (nothing asserted a repository checkpoint does not publish). test_publication_stages_only_the_five_allowlisted_files seeds all five state files plus an unrelated scratch file and a non-allowlisted .bridge_state file, then asserts HEAD contains EXACTLY the five and the unrelated file survives unpublished and undestroyed; mutating the allowlist to git add -A drives it RED, verified. test_repository_checkpoints_never_publish_independently asserts save()/save_retired() leave HEAD and the index untouched while the local files really land. (2) ADR 0099 written (289 lines) recording all nine decisions. The ADR subagent caught THREE corrections to my brief and was right on all three: my 'two of three slices landed' was wrong (only S1's CODE landed - T1 and T2 of S1's three tasks; S2 and S3 are open), 'sole owner of the four files' is SUBSYSTEM-scoped because src/rebar/_ids.py::_resolve_via_binding_store still opens bindings.json for a best-effort READ-ONLY reverse lookup during CLI id resolution and the GHA commit-back commits the same files (both exemptions are now named rather than overclaimed), and config_ownership_exceptions.py has TWO binding_store.py entries to re-register in S2, not one - matching the coordinator independently. A third file, docs/adr/.numbers/0099, was unavoidable: the ADR-to-marker bijection gate requires it and it is generated by scripts/gen_adr_index.py. It is NOT in T3's recorded file_impact, so noting it here. GATES: make lint 0 (both config gates included), typecheck 565 Success, 410 tests pass across state/ plus the docs-index and ADR-number gates.
